transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-27
Start: 09:34 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM); Aisha Khan (Spectra Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (VP Eng), Priya Patel (DevOps), Evan Moore (SRE)

Summary: quick QBR / health check. Covering last quarter usage, cost, a couple of reliability incidents in Feb, and discussing Dedicated pilot and next steps.

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. quick intro from us — I'm Lena, AE, Marco is our SE, Jordan's joining for the QBR. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Aisha: Hey Lena, good thanks. busy but excited to run through this — we've got Tom and Priya with me.
[00:18] Tom: Morning all.
[00:20] Marco: Morning. I'll jump into the perf numbers later but high level we're seeing steady usage and a couple ideas to lower per-token cost.
[00:28] Jordan: we'll cover adoption metrics and a couple of asks from your side at the end.

[00:35] Lena: Cool. quick agenda: usage & spend, reliability incidents, ops questions (VPC/KMS), Dedicated sizing recommendation and next steps. anything to add?
[00:44] Priya: maybe a short bit on network peering and whether we need an express route — we've had some variability in tail latency.
[00:50] Lena: good call.

--- Usage and Cost (00:55 - 12:10) ---
[00:55] Jordan: pulling up the numbers — yr-over-yr? sorry, quarter-over-quarter, last 90 days you were at about 1.8B tokens ingested, monthly avg about 600M tokens, with March spiking to 820M due to a new recommendation model in prod.
[01:14] Aisha: yeah that spike lines up with us turning on the recs model; response lengths are longer there. we're seeing p50 latencies in prod at ~220ms and p95 around 620ms.
[01:26] Marco: ok, that's useful. on cost, your spending is trending 18% above the baseline last quarter. biggest lever is batching/quantization on the recs workload, and also prefix caching for the parts that are identical across requests.
[01:40] Tom: quick q: our engineers tried the 4-bit quantized variant and saw some degradation on quality on certain prompts, it's subtle but laning tests showed 2-3% lower accuracy in our evals.
[01:52] Marco: that's expected; quantization tradeoffs depend on model and prompt fidelity. we can propose a mixed approach — keep FP16 for mission critical route and quantize the lower sensitivity ones. also suggest running the Redwood Optimize guide on your workload; we'll include a recommended profile.
[02:10] Aisha: can you share an actual cost model? we need to present to procurement.
[02:15] Lena: yes, we'll send a Dedicated sizing + cost comparison versus hosted; includes projected monthly cost at current usage and with 20% growth.
[02:24] Jordan: and we'll show break-even assuming a 70% utilization of reserved capacity.

--- Reliability and Incidents (12:11 - 26:00) ---
[12:11] Evan: quick background: we had two incidents in February, one was a region failover and one was a spike causing degraded p95. both were short but impacted the recs pipeline.
[12:25] Marco: looking at the logs you shared, the first was a routing fallback that hit a cold model variant which increased cold-starts, and the spike correlated with a sudden traffic burst with long sequences that exceeded the expected batch cutter window.
[12:38] Aisha: the cold-start showed up as increased tail latency — any suggestions to avoid that?
[12:44] Marco: yes, we recommend warm pools + prefix/KV cache priming for the heavy routes. on Dedicated you can configure warm actors and persistent KV cache to avoid cold starts; that was one of the main reasons customers move to Dedicated.
[12:58] Priya: network jitter seems to amplify tails — is that something Redwood can diagnose from our side or do we need to open a ticket with our infra?
[13:07] Marco: usually we need a pcap or traceroutes to correlate; we can run a joint network test. we'll also provide instrumentation snippets for your side to surface exact hop latencies.
[13:20] Tom: is there an SLA for p95 on Dedicated?
[13:23] Lena: our Dedicated contracts include SLA targets; typical p95 SLOs are 600ms for the models we've benchmarked but it's configurable based on model choice and region. we'll share the SLA doc.

--- Security & Compliance (26:01 - 33:10) ---
[26:01] Aisha: procurement asked about data residency and KMS. we need to ensure keys stay in our control and audit logs are shipped to our SIEM.
[26:10] Lena: for Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed KMS and audit log exports. we also have SOC 2 Type II evidence and can share an ISO27001 questionnaire.
[26:22] Priya: any gotchas with VPC peering? e.g., route propagation or egress costs?
[26:29] Marco: main gotcha is MTU and NAT rules; we typically see route propagation issues when teams have overlapping CIDR ranges — we'll review your network diagram. egress costs depend on cloud region — we'll call that out in the cost model.
[26:43] Tom: how long to set up Dedicated pilot?
[26:46] Lena: pilot usually 2-4 weeks for a minimal sizing: we provision a reserved pool, run perf tests with your payload, and iterate on batching/quant profiles. full production lift could be 8-12 weeks depending on compliance gates.

--- Dedicated Sizing & Benchmarks (33:11 - 44:40) ---
[33:11] Marco: sharing the proposed config: 4xA100-ish nodes for initial pilot, autoscaling for peak, warm pools enabled, and local persistent KV cache. that maps to your peak of ~3K rps during batch window.
[33:28] Aisha: does that include the recs model and a smaller chat assistant model? we have two routes.
[33:33] Marco: yes we modeled two routes: the recs model at 2.2B tokens/day and chat at 400M tokens/day. allocations can be tuned with route-level priorities.
[33:45] Evan: curious about continuous batching impact on latency — our p95 concerns are mostly during peak.
[33:52] Marco: continuous batching is organized to hit throughput while honoring latency SLOs; we can set max batch wait time to cap tail latency. in practice we saw 10-20% cost savings with minimal p95 impact for similar workloads.
[34:08] Priya: about quantization — can you do mixed-precision at route-level?
[34:12] Marco: yes, route-level quant profiles are supported. also suggest running a small AB test to validate quality.
[34:20] Tom: what about fallbacks — if Dedicated is full, do requests go to Hosted?
[34:24] Lena: we offer routing policies — fail open to hosted or to a cheaper model variant. that's configurable per customer.

--- Questions & Open Items (44:41 - 50:30) ---
[44:41] Aisha: one more — our security wants to see an integration checklist. can Jordan own that?
[44:47] Jordan: yep I can assemble a checklist (SAML, KMS, VPC, audit logs, PIE/PII controls) and share.
[44:53] Priya: also need a detailed network diagram, I'll send ours to Marco.
[44:58] Marco: perfect, we'll do a joint runbook for the pilot.
[45:04] Tom: can we get a short exec one-pager comparing continuing hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? procurement asked for that.
[45:10] Lena: yes we'll include that in the packet.

--- Recap and Next Steps (50:31 - 52:00) ---
[50:31] Lena: recap: Marco to run benchmarks with your sample payloads; Lena will send cost model and Dedicated sizing; Jordan will share QBR deck and security checklist; Priya to send network diagram. we'll aim to have the pilot kickoff planning meeting week of Apr 13.
[50:49] Aisha: thanks team, that sounds good. appreciate the clarity on warm pools and quantization tradeoffs.
[50:56] Lena: thanks all, we'll follow up with the packets and schedule the deep dive.
[51:02] Tom: thanks.
[51:05] Evan: thanks everyone.
[51:10] Lena: bye.
